Evidence / VIS-FIRM-CONSTRAINTS
Evidence record
When was it measured or observed?2022

Finance is not the only constraint surveyed formal firms report, 2022

01What does this evidence establish?

Among formal firms in the 2022 Yemen Enterprise Survey of seven governorates, 50% named electricity as a business challenge, 46% fuel shortages, 32% transport or road blockades, 30% tax administration or tax rates, 27% political instability and 22% access to finance; 18% named siege and 17% practices of informal competitors, and each of the other eight challenges listed was named by 15% or fewer, down to 0% for crime, theft and disorder. Firms could name more than one challenge, so the shares add up to more than 100%, and neither the number of firms answering nor the exact question wording is recorded in the evidence base. These results apply to the survey sample in seven governorates and are not a national ranking for all Yemeni firms.

Another view of the evidence
01What does this evidence establish?02What does it measure?03Who or what does it apply to?04How current is it?05What this evidence does not establish06Original source and verification07Method and verification detail

02What does it measure?

The share of surveyed formal firms in seven governorates that named each item as a business challenge, 2022.

03Who or what does it apply to?

Formal enterprises in seven selected governorates covered by the 2022 Yemen Enterprise Survey

04How current is it?

The latest observation in this record refers to the 2022 survey (September 2022). It should not be read as describing a later period unless a newer comparable observation is published.

05What this evidence does not establish

The shares describe formal firms in the 2022 Yemen Enterprise Survey of seven governorates; they are not a national ranking of business constraints for all Yemeni firms. They follow the source's own item wording and can count more than one challenge per firm, so they are not comparable with the 'biggest obstacle' indicator of the World Bank's standard Enterprise Surveys.

Limits of the measure

Firms could name more than one challenge, so the shares add up to more than 100%. Neither the number of firms answering nor the exact question wording is recorded in the evidence base.

07Method and verification detail

Detail for reproducing or challenging this record without changing what it means.

How was it produced?

The formal-firm sample of the World Bank's 2022 Yemen Enterprise Survey, conducted in seven governorates (September 2022) and reported in Yemen Financial Sector Diagnostics (2024). The shares are the source's own tabulation in Annex III, Table 8 ('List of Challenges to the Establishment'), p. 146. On the same page, the source's chart of the six most often named challenges (Figure 108, 'Challenges in Business Environment') gives a different share for transport or road blockades; the table's value is used. Elsewhere the source tabulates the same survey differently: its chart of the top constraints cited by formal firms (Figure 83, p. 111) puts access to finance level with political instability, behind electricity, and its text on p. 145 says access to finance 'remained on top of the main challenges'. Neither is used here. Firms could name more than one challenge.
